status: qualified local public native SDK fixture host; task closure audited separately
scope: Local macOS arm64 isolated stock server, public HTTP SDK administration and Session controls, own signed QUIC Endpoints and actual native PCMU audio. The independent backend is a local synthetic device, with no application Store access or dispatch replacement. No network provider or model result.
implementation: PublicPcmuBridge owns the already negotiated public native peer and explicitly selected PcmuDevice. PCMU is 8kHz mono, 160 bytes/20ms. It holds one pending device frame and bounds writes/cleanup; native substrate queues retain their separate SDK limits.

SignedNativeEndpoint host manifest is distinct from the InProcessAi backend transport manifest. Local device custody grants no Conversation permission. Endpoint enrollment, explicit Session acceptance and current authorized stream selection occur through public interfaces.

Drain keeps its original join handle across caller cancellation, caches terminal reports and failed worker joins, and separately reports native/device cleanup. Drop requests stop; it is not cleanup proof. No command retry, alternate substrate or automatic reconnect is introduced.

behaviors: Actual root-to-device PCMU marker decodes in the independent adapter and the reverse fixture marker decodes in the SDK receiver; repeated original local admission retains one effect.

Cancelling an in-flight bridge drain retains the same cleanup worker. A later drain observes both resources drained, replays the report and calls the device drain once. Retired local original admission cannot reactivate.
Malformed real device frames produce InvalidFrame, zero submissions and confirmed cleanup of the actual signed native peer/device.
A deliberate device receive panic requests cancellation. Repeated bridge drains return Transport without repolling a completed failed join or claiming successful cleanup.

A valid enrolled third peer is refused before entering an uninvited Session. The same peer positively decodes its own authorized Session while the original root continues decoding the fixture; forty isolated decoded frames exclude the positive fixture marker.
Both existing local message functions and both Prism functions pass on the current shared setup and current service permissions.

Actual server shutdown ends the old peer and the bridge drains its original device once. Restart preserves the original completed operation receipt. Same-ID replay cannot construct a new physical peer; explicit fresh Connection IDs establish actual decoded media again.

Endpoint withdrawal refuses a fresh offer. The still-running host attempts at least twenty new marker frames after withdrawal; native submission counters cover those frames (at most one pending), but the independent receiver never decodes that new marker during the bounded observation. Signaling authentication is separate; explicit owner drain confirms cleanup.

A real signed native answer and server callback are deliberately left unconfirmed. After owned client/server shutdown and restart, public operation.get recovers Failed under the original record ID. Exact original replay cannot acquire a new peer or change that recovered operation.
retained_failures: Initial production strip ran out of disk; aggregate qualification was rejected. Closed generated cache variants were losslessly archived with decoded hashes/modes/closure audits, and the current production targets rebuilt successfully.
Initial native setup omitted explicit subscriptions, exposing the named stream-credential floor bug; the separate credential checkpoint fixes and verifies that floor without event rights.

Initial assertions sampled startup silence; the final tests wait for actual markers and continuously pace positive-control sources while checking isolation. The exclusion assertion remains active for every observed isolated frame.

Standalone service feature-graph compilation was interrupted, and the component runner timed out waiting for its build lock; neither is counted as a pass. The shared credential regression passed in the production server graph.
The first HTTP attempt used a Python without jsonschema and failed before runtime. The existing validation environment completed the current 280-case run.
The initial recovery test used a helper trait private to another test module; it now uses the public SDK receive method.

The initial withdrawal assertion expected the physical signaling connection to close. The actual contract fences current media while independent signaling authentication can remain valid. The final test positively exercises media before withdrawal, submits a new marker only after withdrawal, forbids unexpected receiver errors, and explicitly drains the owned bridge.

The strengthened build initially hit objcopy ENOSPC and was rejected. Closed generated cache variants and superseded executables were losslessly archived with closure/hash/mode audits; the corrupt derived target/fingerprint was preserved and invalidated before the successful frozen build.
